trip.hotelsIntro: All Marriott Bonvoy. Ranked for this family: how likely a Titanium/Platinum member is to get a suite (from Flyert 飞客, SMZDM, Trip.com, TripAdvisor and FlyerTalk reports), how new the hotel is, and the location. Vote for one in each city.
trip.hotelsTip: Rooms for 10: plan on 4–5 rooms, with connecting rooms for each family and a room near the lift for the grandparents. Hotels in China often limit rooms to 2 adults + 1 child, so confirm the cot, extra bed and kids' breakfast rules when you book.
trip.about: Flights MH526 / MH527 are booked; exact times are on the e-ticket. Trains, vans and hotels are not booked yet and are marked tentative. Map opens the place in 高德地图 Amap, Google Maps or Apple Maps, in a new tab. Everything is saved in this browser only: no accounts, no server.

elite: Book each room under a different Platinum/Titanium member's own Bonvoy account, with that person staying in the room. Upgrades, lounge access and breakfast go to the member in the room, so 5 rooms means 5 separate chances at a suite.
Book direct on Marriott.com or the Bonvoy app. Most third-party bookings (Trip.com, Agoda) don't get elite benefits.
Titanium members: put Suite Night Awards on the rooms that matter most (the grandparents' room and the room with the baby). They're confirmed a few days before arrival.

About 1–2 weeks before, email the hotel: a multi-generational family of 10, all Titanium/Platinum, 5 rooms. Ask for connecting or adjacent rooms, suites if available, a cot, and how many people can use the lounge per room.
Chengdu is one hotel with a 3-night + 2-night split: ask them to note the upgrade on both bookings, so you return to the same suite on 19 Dec.
Check the breakfast and lounge rules for children when you book; hotels often cap it at the member plus one guest, and kids' rules vary.
Since 2025 Marriott only promises "an upgrade", not a suite, and upgrades in China are now decided by an algorithm, so treat suites as likely, not guaranteed.

days.label: Family's pick: day trip or city
Last day · fly home after midnight

items.name: Lunch — Chen Mapo Tofu 陈麻婆豆腐
items.info: The famous name in mapo tofu (several branches; Map lists them). Order some dishes 微辣 (wēi là, mild) or 不辣 (bù là, no chilli) for the kids and elderly.

items.name: People's Park & Heming Teahouse 人民公园 · 鹤鸣茶社
items.info: Chengdu at its most relaxed: bamboo chairs by the lake, a pot of jasmine tea, ear-cleaners doing the rounds, grandparents dancing. Flat paths all the way round.

items.name: Kuanzhai Alley 宽窄巷子
items.info: Three restored Qing-era lanes of courtyard houses, snacks and tea shops. Flat and pram-friendly; busy after 5pm, so hold small hands.

items.name: Dinner — Sichuan hot pot 火锅
items.info: Ask for a 鸳鸯锅 (yuān yāng guō): a split pot with a spicy side and a clear broth side, so the kids and elderly eat from the mild half. Well-known chains: 小龙坎 Xiaolongkan, 蜀九香 Shu Jiu Xiang (several branches; Map lists them).

items.name: Giant Panda Base 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
items.info: Go at opening: pandas are most active in the cool morning. Use the ¥10 park shuttle bus between enclosures to save little and older legs. The nurseries with cubs are the highlight.
items.mapq: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
items.mapen: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
items.book: Tickets open 14 days ahead (from Tue 1 Dec) on Trip.com or the base's WeChat mini-program; passport for each person. Book the shuttle bus at the same time.

items.name: Lunch — Long Chao Shou wontons 龙抄手
items.info: A Chengdu snack institution on Chunxi Road: wontons in clear or red-oil broth, plus small plates of Chengdu snacks. Gentle food for everyone.

items.name: Back to the hotel — nap & rest
items.info: Early start and a long walk: nap time for the baby and a rest for the elderly before the evening.

items.name: Dinner — Sichuan home cooking
items.info: e.g. 马旺子 Ma Wang Zi. Mild dishes that work for kids: 宫保鸡丁 kung pao chicken, 回锅肉 twice-cooked pork, 蒜蓉空心菜 garlic greens, 蛋炒饭 egg fried rice. Several branches; Map lists them.

items.name: Lunch on the train
items.info: Buy buns and snacks at Chengdu East before boarding, or order a hot meal to your seat when booking on Trip.com / 铁路12306. Hot water taps in every carriage for baby bottles.

items.name: Big Wild Goose Pagoda 大雁塔
items.info: The 7th-century Tang pagoda, beautifully lit at dusk. The squares around it are free and flat; going inside the temple grounds is optional.

items.name: Dinner — Chang'an Da Pai Dang 长安大牌档
items.info: Lively Shaanxi restaurant with the Xi'an classics in one place: roujiamo, biangbiang noodles, liangpi, paomo. Staff in costume; kids love it. Several branches near the pagoda.

items.name: Great Tang All Day Mall night walk 大唐不夜城
items.info: A long pedestrian boulevard of Tang-dynasty light sculptures and street performers running south from the pagoda. Flat and wide, fine for strollers and wheelchairs. Very cold after dark in December.

items.name: Terracotta Army 秦始皇兵马俑
items.info: Start at Pit 1 (the famous rows of 2,000-year-old warriors), then Pits 3 and 2. It's a long walk from the car park to the pits, so pace it for the elderly and bring the baby carrier as well as the stroller. The halls are big and cold in winter.
items.book: Online only, up to 7 days ahead (from Thu 10 Dec); passport for each person. Book a private van for the day, about 1h each way.

items.name: Lunch in Lintong
items.info: Plenty of restaurants near the museum exit. Keep it simple and warm: noodles, dumplings, soup.

items.name: Dinner — De Fa Chang dumpling banquet 德发长饺子宴
items.info: A long-established restaurant by the Bell Tower serving a banquet of dumplings in many shapes and fillings. Soft, not spicy, fun for kids and grandparents alike.

items.name: Shaanxi History Museum 陕西历史博物馆
items.info: One of China's great museums: Tang gold and silver, murals, Zhou bronzes. Warm and indoor, a good morning for everyone after yesterday's walking.
items.book: Free, but reserve with each person's passport on the museum's WeChat / website. Slots are released a few days ahead (reported 5–7 days); watch from Fri 11 Dec. Closed Mondays in winter.

items.name: Lunch — biangbiang noodles & roujiamo
items.info: Xi'an's two signatures: belt-wide hand-pulled noodles, and the "Chinese burger" of braised meat in a crisp bun (樊记腊汁肉夹馍 Fan Ji is the famous one).

items.name: City Wall at South Gate 永宁门
items.info: The most complete old city wall in China, about 14km round and wide enough to cycle. Bikes for the energetic; everyone else strolls a short stretch for the view. There are steps up at the gate, so ask at the ticket office for the easiest way up with the grandparents and the pram.
items.mapen: Yongningmen South Gate Xi'an City Wall

items.name: Bell & Drum Towers 钟楼 · 鼓楼
items.info: The two Ming towers at the heart of the old city, lit up at dusk. Seeing them from the square is free and easy; climbing is optional.

items.name: Lunch at Xi'an North station
items.info: Noodles and buns in the station food court, or pick up food for the train.

items.name: Dinner & Chunxi Road by night 春熙路
items.info: Walk to the shopping streets for Christmas lights and street snacks: 钟水饺 Zhong dumplings, 糖油果子 sugar-fried dough balls, 冰粉 ice jelly.

items.name: Dinner near the hotel
items.info: An easy one after a big day out.

items.name: Lunch — Chengdu snacks 钟水饺 · 担担面
items.info: Sweet-soy Zhong dumplings, dan dan noodles, 赖汤圆 glutinous rice balls. Order a spread and share.

items.name: Rest, showers & pack (keep the rooms)
items.info: The flight leaves after midnight. Keep the rooms until evening (late check-out, or book the night of 21 Dec) so the baby naps and everyone showers before the airport.

items.name: Farewell dinner
items.info: A proper Sichuan banquet to finish: book a private room 包间 for 10. Keep it early; the airport run starts at 21:30.

items.name: Sichuan Opera face-changing show 蜀风雅韵
items.info: Chengdu's classic evening show in a teahouse theatre: face-changing, fire-spitting, shadow puppets, comic sketches. Seats with tea.

items.name: Jinli Street lanterns 锦里
items.info: Red lanterns reflected in the ponds, snack stalls, next to Wuhou Shrine. Pretty and short.

items.name: Early night: jet-lag recovery
items.info: We landed after midnight. Bath, bed.

items.name: Taikoo Li, Daci Temple & the IFS panda 太古里 · 大慈寺
items.info: Low-rise open-air shopping streets around a Buddhist temple, then the giant panda climbing the side of IFS. Christmas lights in December.

items.name: Wuhou Shrine & Jinli 武侯祠 · 锦里
items.info: Memorial temple to the Three Kingdoms heroes (Zhuge Liang, Liu Bei) with red walls and bamboo, then the lantern street next door.

items.name: Hotel pool, lounge & free time
items.info: Swim, tea, naps. Save energy for Xi'an.

items.name: Huaqing Palace 华清宫
items.info: Tang emperors' hot-spring palace at the foot of Mount Li, next to the Terracotta Army. Gardens and pavilions by a lake.

items.name: Back to the hotel to rest
items.info: The Terracotta Army is a long morning on foot. Warm up and nap.

items.name: Muslim Quarter street food 回民街
items.info: The old Hui neighbourhood behind the Drum Tower: lamb skewers, persimmon cakes, sticky rice cake, pomegranate juice. Very crowded, so bring the baby carrier rather than the stroller.

items.name: Tang Dynasty dinner & show 唐乐宫
items.info: Seated dinner from 18:00, then a big costumed Tang-court music and dance show (about 20:15–21:40). Warm, comfortable, no walking.
items.book: Book a few days ahead on Trip.com.

items.name: Yongxingfang food street 永兴坊
items.info: A calmer, tidier food street by the city wall, with snacks from all over Shaanxi.

items.name: Tang costume family photoshoot 唐装 · 汉服
items.info: Rent Tang-style robes near the Big Wild Goose Pagoda and take family portraits. Hair and make-up for 10 is slow, so start at opening, or dress just the kids and a few adults. Back for the 12:00 check-out.

items.name: Small Wild Goose Pagoda & Xi'an Museum 小雁塔 · 西安博物院
items.info: Quiet temple garden with a slender Tang pagoda, and a free city museum in the same grounds. Calm and flat.

items.name: Slow morning, brunch & pack
items.info: Lie-in before the train.

items.name: G-train Chengdu East → Leshan 乐山
items.info: About 1 hour, then 30 min by van to the river pier.
items.book: Train tickets open 15 days ahead counting the travel day: Sun 6 Dec for both the outbound and return trains.

items.name: Leshan Giant Buddha by boat 乐山大佛
items.info: The 71m Buddha carved into a riverside cliff 1,200 years ago. The river boat shows the whole figure with no steps, which is best for the baby and grandparents. The path down beside the Buddha is hundreds of steep steps with long queues; optional for the fit.

items.name: G-train Leshan → Chengdu East
items.info: Taxi or van back to Leshan station after lunch, then about 1 hour to Chengdu East.

items.name: Dujiangyan irrigation system 都江堰
items.info: A 2,200-year-old river engineering wonder that still waters the Chengdu plain: rushing water, suspension bridges and hillside temples, about 1h by van. Some slopes and steps.

items.name: Du Fu Thatched Cottage 杜甫草堂
items.info: Bamboo groves, streams and the poet Du Fu's cottage in a large, calm garden. Flat paths.

items.name: Sichuan Museum 四川博物院
items.info: Right by Du Fu's cottage: Sichuan bronzes, Han pottery, Buddhist sculpture. Free and indoor. Closed Mondays, so Sunday is its day.
items.book: Free with passport; reserve on its WeChat a few days ahead.

items.name: Chengdu Natural History Museum (dinosaurs) 成都自然博物馆
items.info: A huge hall of dinosaur skeletons found in Sichuan, plus minerals and animals. Indoor and warm, made for the kids.
items.book: Reserve on its WeChat a few days ahead; closed Mondays.

items.name: Afternoon tea & rest
items.info: Back to the hotel, or a second round of tea in People's Park.

items.name: Wenshu Monastery 文殊院
items.info: Chengdu's busiest Buddhist temple: incense and quiet courtyards. Its well-known vegetarian restaurant can replace the snack lunch if you prefer.

items.name: Last-minute shopping: IFS & Chunxi Road
items.info: Panda souvenirs, Sichuan pepper and tea to take home.

items.name: Pool & slow morning
items.info: Rest up before the overnight flight.

items.name: Tianfu Square & Chunxi Road 天府广场
items.info: The central square and main shopping street, walkable from the central Marriott hotels.

items.name: Jinsha Site Museum 金沙遗址博物馆
items.info: 3,000-year-old Shu kingdom site, home of the golden Sun Bird. Indoor.

items.name: Mount Qingcheng 青城山
items.info: Misty Taoist mountain with a cable car. Many steps and slippery in winter; for fit adults.

items.name: Tang Paradise 大唐芙蓉园
items.info: A large Tang-style garden by Qujiang Pool, lit at night. Near the W and the Westin.

items.name: Yangrou paomo 羊肉泡馍
items.info: Tear flatbread into lamb broth: Xi'an's soul food. 老孙家 Lao Sun Jia is the classic.

items.name: Biangbiang noodles
items.info: Belt-wide hand-pulled noodles with chilli oil. Ask for less chilli for kids.

items.name: Climb the Drum Tower 鼓楼
items.info: Steep steps up for the drum performance and views over the Muslim Quarter.

decisions.title: Monday evening
decisions.question: After hot pot on the first night, what next?

options.name: Sichuan Opera face-changing
options.blurb: The masks that change in a flash. 1.5h, seats with tea. Late-ish for the baby.

options.name: Jinli lanterns stroll
options.blurb: Short, pretty, lantern-lit old street. About 1 hour.

options.name: Early night
options.blurb: We land after midnight the night before. Sleep wins.

decisions.title: Tuesday late afternoon
decisions.question: After the pandas and a nap:

options.name: Taikoo Li + IFS panda
options.blurb: Shopping streets around an old temple, Christmas lights, the famous climbing panda.

options.name: Wuhou Shrine + Jinli
options.blurb: Three Kingdoms temple and bamboo gardens, then the lantern street.

options.name: Pool & lounge
options.blurb: A quiet afternoon at the hotel.

options.name: Huaqing Palace
options.blurb: Imperial hot-spring gardens nearby, no extra long drive.

options.name: Hotel & rest
options.blurb: Head back, warm up and nap before the dumpling dinner.

options.name: Muslim Quarter food crawl
options.blurb: The famous one: loud, crowded, delicious.

options.name: Tang Dynasty dinner show
options.blurb: Sit-down dinner with a big costumed show. Easiest for the grandparents.

options.name: Yongxingfang food street
options.blurb: Same snacks, fewer crowds, stroller works.

decisions.title: Saturday morning
decisions.question: Before the afternoon train back to Chengdu:

options.name: Tang costume family photos
options.blurb: Dress up in Tang robes for portraits by the pagoda. Early start; hair & make-up for 10 takes a while.

options.name: Small Wild Goose Pagoda
options.blurb: Peaceful garden and free museum.

options.name: Slow morning
options.blurb: Sleep in, brunch, pack.

options.name: Leshan Giant Buddha
options.blurb: Day trip by 1h fast train. See the 71m cliff Buddha from a boat, no stairs needed.

options.name: Dujiangyan
options.blurb: Ancient waterworks, bridges and temples in green hills. 1h by van, some steps.

options.name: Du Fu Cottage + Sichuan Museum
options.blurb: Stay in town: bamboo garden in the morning, museum next door after lunch.

options.name: Dinosaur museum + easy afternoon
options.blurb: Kids' pick: giant Sichuan dinosaurs, then tea and rest.

decisions.title: Monday morning
decisions.question: Last morning (most museums are closed on Mondays):

options.name: Wenshu Monastery
options.blurb: Temple courtyards, incense and ginkgo trees.

options.name: Shopping at IFS & Chunxi Rd
options.blurb: Souvenirs, tea, Sichuan pepper.

options.name: Pool & slow morning
options.blurb: Save energy for the 1am flight.

Chengdu.nights: Sun 13 → Wed 16 Dec (3 nights) and Sat 19 → Mon 21 Dec (2 nights + the evening)
Chengdu.tip: Book the same hotel for both Chengdu stays: leave the big suitcases with the concierge while you're in Xi'an and take only overnight bags and the baby things on the train. Book the first night from Sun 13 Dec and tell the hotel you'll arrive around 1:30am, so the rooms are held.

options.name: JW Marriott Hotel Chengdu
pros: Guests with elite status report upgrades to executive suites
Executive lounge and breakfast for Platinum and Titanium
Walk to Chunxi Road, Taikoo Li and the IFS panda; Tianfu Square metro nearby
cons: About 10 years old by the trip, with no major renovation found
Busy shopping district, lively outside at night

gallery.cap: Taikoo Li shopping streets · short walk

options.upnote: TripAdvisor: Titanium and Ambassador guests upgraded to executive suites with a separate bedroom and two bathrooms. The lounge is included for Platinum and above.

options.name: W Chengdu
pros: Newest in Chengdu (2020)
Reported to upgrade generously, often to a suite (panda-themed WOW / Fantastic suites)
South side: a shorter drive to Tianfu Airport
cons: No executive lounge: the elite perk is a lobby-bar happy hour
25–35 min by car to the old-town sights

gallery.cap: Chengdu Financial City · the hotel's district

options.upnote: SMZDM (Platinum): "generous with upgrades, basically a suite when availability allows". Elites get a lobby-bar happy hour, with no lounge.

options.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Chengdu

pros: Beautiful suites and Club floors over Tianfu Square (55 suites)
Short ride to People's Park, Kuanzhai and Chunxi Road
cons: Platinum members get no Club Lounge or free breakfast at Ritz-Carlton
Ritz-Carlton suite upgrades are hard even for Titanium

gallery.cap: Tianfu Square · the hotel overlooks it

options.upnote: Reviewers advise Platinum members to pick the JW or St. Regis, since the Ritz gives them no lounge or breakfast. Suites are possible for Titanium but not dependable.

options.name: The St. Regis Chengdu
options.address: 88 Taisheng Road South 太升南路88号
pros: Spacious rooms and butler service
Close to Tianfu Square and Chunxi Road

Xi'an.tip: Stay in Qujiang, near the Big Wild Goose Pagoda and the night-walk street. The W and the Westin are both there, a short ride apart. Mid-December is low season in Xi'an, which helps the upgrade odds.

options.name: W Xi'an
options.address: 333 Qujiang Chi East Road 曲江池东路333号
pros: Built 2018: much newer than the Westin
A Jan 2025 Flyert stay was upgraded to a 100+ m² suite by default (free minibar)
Very good breakfast; by Qujiang Pool park and Tang Paradise, a short ride to the pagoda
cons: Lively W vibe with a nightclub
Further from the old city wall and the Muslim Quarter

options.upnote: Flyert (Jan 2025): "suite upgrade by default, without asking or a suite certificate". TripAdvisor: a suite upgrade for a Marriott elite guest.

gallery.cap: Big Wild Goose Pagoda · next door

prep: Now
Vote on hotels, then book each room direct under a different Platinum/Titanium member (tips in the Hotels tab). Ask for connecting rooms and a baby cot.
Now
Passports valid 6+ months. Malaysians currently enter China visa-free for up to 30 days; re-check nearer the date.
Now
Set up Alipay (and/or WeChat Pay) with a Malaysian card and get China eSIMs. Install 高德 Amap, Didi and Trip.com.
Tue 1 Dec
Panda Base tickets + shuttle bus for Tue 15 Dec (14 days ahead).
Wed 2 Dec
Train tickets to Xi'an for Wed 16 Dec (rail sales open 15 days ahead, counting the travel day).
Sat 5 Dec
Train back Xi'an → Chengdu for Sat 19 Dec.
Sun 6 Dec
Leshan trains, there and back, for Sun 20 Dec, if Leshan wins the vote.
By 6 Dec
Book vans: Tianfu Airport pickup ~00:15 Mon 14 Dec (10 people + luggage + pram), the Terracotta day van, and the 21:30 airport run on Mon 21 Dec.
Thu 10 Dec
Terracotta Army tickets for Thu 17 Dec (online only, 7 days ahead, passports).
Fri 11 Dec
Start watching for Shaanxi History Museum slots for Fri 18 Dec (free, passport per person, released a few days ahead).
Pack

Chengdu is about 5–12°C and damp; Xi'an about −3–8°C and dry. Thermals, gloves and beanies for everyone; a pram cover and baby carrier; tissues (many toilets have none); the grandparents' medicines in hand luggage.
